title: Dispatch: linear paren-scan repair for three polynomial-ReDoS sites (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch bead for `eshyra-e1kt` (read that bead for the spec). Attempt 1.

Branch/worktree: `eshyra-e1kt.1`, cut from branch `eshyra-e1kt`.
Model config: gpt-5.6-luna, reasoning effort medium.

## What CodeQL actually flags

Three open `js/polynomial-redos` alerts (#15, #16, #17), all the SAME
recognizer shape — `/\([^)]*\)/`. The alert message is "may run slow on
strings starting with '(' and with many repetitions of '('": `[^)]` admits
`(`, so the inner star overlaps the `\(` prefix. On `"((((((..."` (no `)`)
every start position rescans to end of string — O(n^2).

- `packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:259` — inside
  `normalizeAbilityName`: `.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ')`
- `packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:353` — inside
  `economyFromEntryMechanics`: `entryName.replace(/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/, '')`.
  Alert 17 reports TWO findings for this one line: the `(` overlap above, and
  a second on "many repetitions of ' '" from the leading `\s*` against the
  `$`-anchored tail.
- `packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:441` — inside
  `normalizeLegendaryName`: `.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ')`

## Reachability — fix, do not dismiss

These are not fed only by the bundled SRD pack. `normalizeAbilityName` is
called on caller-supplied `input.ability` (`usageCounters.ts:851`, `:1024`)
and `normalizeLegendaryName` on `input.legendaryActionName`
(`actionEconomy.ts:1183`) — i.e. tool-call arguments from the model/DM path,
plus arbitrary third-party rules-pack record text. The "trusted and fixed
size" escape hatch in the parent bead does not apply to any of the three.

The neighbouring `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')` (usageCounters:262) and
`.trim()` (actionEconomy:444) are NOT flagged and must not be touched: the
preceding `.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, …)` already collapses separator runs to a
single character, so those quantifiers can never span more than one char.
`LEGENDARY_COUNT_RE` (actionEconomy:428) is likewise unflagged and out of
scope — its `\d+` sits behind the literal prefix `take `.

## Required fix shape — linear scan, behavior preserved

Precedent in this repo: commit `bf075b8` (`hasMechanicalParenNote` in
`packages/core/src/rules/srdPlayabilityAudit.ts`) replaced the same recognizer
shape with an `indexOf`-based scan, and `d4462b6` did the same for the
encounter-combatant slug. Follow that, not a bounded-repetition patch: an
`indexOf` scan reproduces the regex EXACTLY, where `\([^()]*\)` or
`\([^)]{0,N}\)` would silently change results on nested or overlong input.

Add one small shared module — suggested
`packages/core/src/state/parentheticalNames.ts` — with two exported helpers,
both pure and allocation-light, each carrying a comment that names the CodeQL
rule and states the equivalence it preserves. Both call sites in
`usageCounters.ts` and the one in `actionEconomy.ts` then import it; do not
duplicate the scan in two files.

1. `replaceParentheticals(text: string, replacement: string): string`
   — exact equivalent of `text.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, replacement)`.
   Because `[^)]*` cannot cross a `)`, each match runs from a `(` to the
   FIRST `)` after it, and the global scan resumes just past that `)`:

   ```ts
   let out = '';
   let from = 0;
   for (;;) {
     const open = text.indexOf('(', from);
     if (open === -1) break;
     const close = text.indexOf(')', open + 1);
     if (close === -1) break;   // no ')' after open ⇒ none after any later '('
     out += text.slice(from, open) + replacement;
     from = close + 1;
   }
   return out + text.slice(from);
   ```

2. `stripTrailingParenthetical(text: string): string`
   — exact equivalent of `text.replace(/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/, '')`.
   That regex takes the leftmost match, which forces the `(` to be the last
   `(` in the string, the closing `)` to be the last non-space character, and
   the span between them to contain no `)`; the leading `\s*` then eats the
   whole whitespace run before that `(`. So:

   ```ts
   const end = text.trimEnd().length;          // JS \s and trim share a set
   if (end === 0 || text[end - 1] !== ')') return text;
   const open = text.lastIndexOf('(', end - 1);
   if (open === -1) return text;
   if (text.slice(open + 1, end - 1).includes(')')) return text;
   return text.slice(0, open).trimEnd();
   ```

   Note `String.prototype.trim`/`trimEnd` strip exactly WhiteSpace ∪
   LineTerminator, the same set `\s` matches, so the `\s*` ↔ `trimEnd`
   substitution is faithful — say so in the comment.

Export both from `packages/core/src/internal.ts` (new core symbols default to
internal per AGENTS.md § Conventions; do NOT add them to `index.ts`).

## Tests

Add a new `packages/core/test/parentheticalNames.test.ts` importing the two
helpers from `../src/internal.js`, covering:

- **Differential equivalence.** A shared fixture list of ordinary and edge
  inputs — `'Fire Breath (Recharge 5-6)'`, `'Cone of Cold (3/Day)'`,
  `'a (x) b (y)'`, `'a (x) y)'`, `'(x)'`, `'unclosed ( paren'`, `'no parens'`,
  `''`, `'  (trailing)   '`, `'nested (a (b) c)'`, `'(a)(b)'` — asserted equal
  to the ORIGINAL regexes (`/\([^)]*\)/g`, `/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/`) evaluated
  inline in the test. This is the "behavior identical" evidence; keep the
  original regexes visible in the test file as the oracle.
- **Adversarial long input, one per flagged site.** Build
  `'('.repeat(200_000)` (and, for the `\s*` finding on line 353,
  `' '.repeat(200_000) + '(x'`) and assert each helper returns the expected
  value AND that the call completes inside a generous wall-clock budget
  (e.g. `expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(1_000)`). The budget is
  deliberately loose — it must separate linear from quadratic, not measure
  performance; a quadratic scan on 200k characters takes minutes.

Also add one adversarial regression per PUBLIC site so the fix is anchored to
the real call paths, in the existing suites:

- `packages/core/test/usageCounters.test.ts` — a spend/reset call whose
  `input.ability` is the adversarial `'('.repeat(200_000)` string, asserting
  it fails closed with the ordinary "no such counter" error promptly rather
  than hanging. Match whatever error shape that path already produces; read
  the surrounding tests first and reuse their `setup()`/fixture helpers.
- `packages/core/test/actionEconomy.test.ts` — the same for
  `input.legendaryActionName` on the legendary-action spend path
  (`actionEconomy.ts:1183`).
- If a per-day display name is reachable in the existing usage-counter suite,
  add an `entryName` fixture with a trailing parenthetical plus a long
  whitespace run to cover line 353's second finding through the real path.

Do not weaken or delete any existing assertion to accommodate the change; the
outputs for all real SRD names must be byte-identical.

## Verification

From the worktree root: `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing (it
rewrites files). All non-skipped tests must pass; the documented skips are the
live-API integration tests and the Dolt-gated checkpoint tests.

## Out of scope

No change to usage-counter or action-economy semantics, no change to counter
keys or display-name text for any real input, no touching the unflagged
regexes named above, no CodeQL configuration or alert-dismissal changes.
